source: MAFF Department of Agricultural Extension / ASPIRE Project, IFAD-funded - "ដំណាំក្រូចថ្លុង" (Pomelo Cultivation Guide), 2017, 90pp
text:
For marcotting (ការធ្វើមេក), farmers select a healthy, disease-free branch about the thickness of a thumb, free of pests, with no cracks in the bark. A ring of bark roughly 15 mm x 30 mm is removed to interrupt nutrient flow and trigger root formation at that point.

Materials needed for the technique include: coconut husk fiber or moss as a moist rooting medium, a bucket to soak the medium, a sharp knife for ring-barking, plastic sheeting to wrap the moistened medium around the wound, and wire or string to tie both ends of the wrapping securely so moisture is retained and the medium is not dislodged by wind or rain.

The prepared marcot is left on the tree for roughly 2 to 3 months. Growers should choose a wound diameter appropriate to the branch and avoid marcotting from branches that are too young (no flower buds yet) or too old (thick, woody growth that roots poorly).
